topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: Defocused reflectors amplify path loss and signal interference, directly impacting SNR, requiring higher SNR to achieve equivalent performance compared to conventional designs. This increased path loss leads to multipath propagation, reducing signal quality and capacity.  Conventional reflectors offer robustness against failures, but require higher SNR for equivalent performance.  The trade-off necessitates careful design choices to optimize link budget margins while considering receiver noise floor characteristics.
